text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Balkan Transport study financed by PHARE programme presented at the regional meeting of "Group of 24" in Skopje on Tuesday gains support from Albania, Bulgaria, Croatia, Bosnia and Macedonia. EU delegation expressed readiness to finance separate projects. Macedonia especially interested in the East-West corridor.

- Dutch Minister for Development and Cooperation Jan Pronk stated at press conference on Tuesday that the Netherlands "will help Macedonia overcome its debt of $35 million to European Investment Bank at the donors conference at the end of February in Brussels".

- French Minister for European Issues Michel Barnier stated in Skopje on Tuesday that France "will support the EU agreement on trade and cooperation with Macedonia. Macedonia is a country with a European orientation and leads politics that contributes to peace in the region".
- All Macedonian tourist agencies have cancelled arrangements with Bulgaria because of demonstrations and general political situation in this neighbouring country.

- Fadil Sulejmani, rector of illegal Tetovo university who was recently released from jail, told Dnevnik that "Tetovo university is a Macedonian university and this state should recognize it. It should not be a private university and the state should finance it".
